subject: Re: AcmeHealth onboarding — MSA/Order Form redlines + DPA/SCCs alignment
body:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeHealth onboarding — first pass redlines (MSA + Order Form) + DPA

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is our first consolidated pass on the MSA and Order Form with inline redlines. We flagged two DPA/GDPR areas where we need explicit alignment before legal signs:

- Roles: the redline proposes a controller-to-processor mapping but we need explicit language for processor subprocessor notice windows.
- SCCs: we included standard Module Two language but would like confirmation Redwood will maintain KMS controls for any EU data; also asking about the fallback hosting region if US hosting is unavailable.
- Transfer impact addendum: our procurement team asked for a draft addendum to capture transit responsibilities for logs/diagnostics.

Can you coordinate with your legal/ops to confirm whether:
1) Redwood can accept the processor/subprocessor notice timeframe (30 days) or propose an alternative;
2) whether the SCCs reference sheet can be attached as an exhibit (we attached a suggested matrix); and
3) whether Redwood has a standard transfer-impact addendum we can reuse.

We'd like to get this to final redlines by EOD Friday if possible — expiry of our internal timeline.

Attachments: Acme_Redlines_v3.docx (docx), SCCs_reference_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Sara Jensen
Head of Procurement | AcmeHealth Inc.
privacy@acmehealth.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth onboarding — first pass redlines (MSA + Order Form) + DPA

Hi Sara — thanks for the packet and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (infra/ops) to confirm technical and legal constraints. Quick read-through and proposed next steps below.

Proposed internal split of work:
- Legal (Laura): take the MSA/order form redlines and produce a mark-up with a clear recommendation on processor/subprocessor notice and the SCCs exhibit approach.
- Infra/ops (Karthik): validate KMS / hosting commitments, draft a short transfer-impact addendum template if we have one, and confirm the fallback region policy.
- Commercial (me): coordinate timelines with Acme and consolidate a single follow-up to keep your Friday target.

Initial answers to your asks (high-level):
1) Processor/subprocessor notice (30 days) — we typically request 14 days for non-emergency notices and 30 days for contractual changes tied to onboarding subprocessors. We can propose a middle path in negotiation (15–21 days) but will confirm with legal.
2) SCCs exhibit — acceptable in principle; we prefer Redwood-controlled exhibit that references our verified model hosting footprint and a binding KMS clause. Laura will recommend the exact exhibit language.
3) Transfer-impact addendum — Redwood has a lightweight template for transfer risk acknowledgements; Karthik will check whether it needs an operations appendix for log transfer responsibilities.

Can everyone aim to have internal comments back by Wed EOD so I can send consolidated responses to Acme on Thu? If Friday finalization is non-negotiable on your side, we can compress but will need signoff from legal for any concessions.

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Grant
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

-----Original Message-----
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 11:20:43 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth onboarding — first pass redlines (MSA + Order Form) + DPA

Thanks Michael / Sara (cc'd) — I had a quick scan and a couple of priority decision points for legal:

1) Roles and data flows — need the list of categories of data (PII, healthcare PHI-ish flags) in the Order Form to calibrate liability clauses. If Acme can provide the sample data mapping, that would speed review.
2) Subprocessor notice window — legal preference is 14 calendar days for routine onboarding + immediate notice for emergency/security-driven replacements. We can accept 30 days only if there is a carveout for emergency security patches.
3) SCCs exhibit — we will attach an exhibit referencing the standard EU SCC Module Two + an operations matrix describing KMS custody. Please confirm which KMS provider and region binding you expect Acme to rely on.

I will produce a marked DPA based on Redwood_DPA_template_v2.docx and track redlines in Track Changes. If Karthik can confirm the ops items below, I'll try to have a draft back to Michael by Wed morning.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:30:55 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth onboarding — first pass redlines (MSA + Order Form) + DPA

Quick infra ops notes (cc'ing product security for visibility):

- KMS: Redwood uses a customer-isolated KMS by default for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API customers, we offer tenant-level envelope keys backed by AWS KMS (us-east-1). We can commit to key custody controls but need to confirm whether Acme requires customer-managed keys (CMK) or Redwood-managed keys.
- Hosting / fallback: Primary hosting will be US (us-east-1). We do have documented fallback to eu-west-1 for resilience; however, cross-border failover is considered an exceptional event and requires a contractual clause (we can provide a transfer-impact addendum to capture that behavior).
- Subprocessors: the current public subprocessor list is stable; any new onboarding follows a 14-day notice window in our standard practice. For security emergency replacements we can notify post-action with retroactive documentation.

I'll attach SCCs_reference_matrix.xlsx with the column that maps our default infra commitments to the SCC clauses. Will follow up if we need more details on the data categories.

-Karthik
Infra Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth onboarding — first pass redlines (MSA + Order Form) + DPA

Sara / Acme team — thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps below (consolidated):

1) Roles / Notice windows
- Redwood legal proposes: 14 days notice for standard subprocessor onboarding; immediate notice for security/emergency replacements with retroactive confirmation. Laura will mark the MSA to reflect this.

2) SCCs / KMS
- We can accept an SCCs exhibit; Redwood will attach its standard SCCs matrix as an exhibit and include binding KMS custody language. For Hosted API, KMS is Redwood-managed in us-east-1 by default; we can discuss CMKs for Dedicated. Karthik attached the infra matrix for reference.

3) Transfer-impact addendum
- Karthik confirmed we have a short transfer-impact addendum template — ops annex will capture log/diagnostic transfer responsibilities and fallback-region behavior. Laura will include the addendum as an exhibit to the Order Form.

4) Timeline
- Laura: draft DPA + MSA mark by Wed EOD (she'll try for Wed morning).
- Karthik: finalize SCCs matrix + ops annex by Wed EOD.
- Michael: consolidate and send to Acme on Thu for review; target to close legal comment cycle by Fri EOD.

Attachments included for your review: Redwood_DPA_template_v2.docx (docx), SCCs_reference_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Related links: DocuSign will be used for signature in the final stage — I will send a DocuSign envelope after we lock the Order Form.

If anything is blocking on Acme's side (e.g., irrevocable internal timeline to sign by Fri), please let me know now so we can prioritize.

Best regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
